Proposition
[Orthonormal Frames for Pseudo-Riemannian Manifolds]

↗ def:pseudo-riemannian-metric ↗ lem:completion-nondegenerate-bases ↗ lem:sections-through-prescribed-basis ↗ lem:open-nondegenerate-tuple ↗ prop:orthonormalize-nondegenerate-family

1. ch2:2.66

Every point of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold has a neighborhood carrying a smooth orthonormal frame.

Proof

↗ lem:completion-nondegenerate-bases ↗ lem:sections-through-prescribed-basis ↗ lem:open-nondegenerate-tuple ↗ prop:orthonormalize-nondegenerate-family ↗ lem:pseudo-metric-fibre-scalar-product \sketch Complete the empty tuple to a nondegenerate basis of $T_pM$. Extend this basis to smooth local vector fields and shrink the neighborhood so their leading Gram determinants remain nonzero. Proposition 16.3 then produces $n$ smooth orthonormal vector fields, which form a frame in each $n$-dimensional tangent space.

□

Proof

↗ prop:orthonormal-frames-pseudo-riemannian ↗ lem:completion-nondegenerate-bases ↗ lem:sections-through-prescribed-basis ↗ lem:open-nondegenerate-tuple ↗ prop:orthonormalize-nondegenerate-family ↗ lem:pseudo-metric-fibre-scalar-product

\sketch This is the preceding proposition.

□

For $r,s\geq 0$, the pseudo-Euclidean space $\mathbb R^{r,s}$ is $\mathbb R^{r+s}$ with coordinates $(\xi ^1,\ldots ,\xi ^r,\tau ^1,\ldots ,\tau ^s)$ and metric \begin{equation} \bar g^{(r,s)}=(d\xi ^1)^2+\cdots +(d\xi ^r)^2 -(d\tau ^1)^2-\cdots -(d\tau ^s)^2. \tag {2.24} \end{equation}
